options.text: Automatic request validation and typed parsing of the body

items.stem: When is declaring a FastAPI path operation with async def a poor choice?

options.text: When the handler performs blocking CPU-bound work
options.rationale: Correct: blocking work in an async handler stalls the event loop; use a thread/process pool.

options.text: When calling an async database client
options.rationale: That is an ideal use of async.

options.text: When awaiting an HTTP request to another service
options.rationale: I/O awaits are exactly what async is for.
Return type does not dictate sync vs async.

items.explanation: Correct: blocking work in an async handler stalls the event loop; use a thread/process pool.

items.stem: Which statements comparing Flask and FastAPI are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: FastAPI generates OpenAPI docs automatically from type hints and models
options.rationale: Correct: interactive docs come for free from the declarations.

options.text: Flask is a WSGI framework while FastAPI is built on ASGI
options.rationale: Correct: this underlies their concurrency models.

options.text: Flask validates request bodies automatically from type hints
options.rationale: False; Flask needs explicit validation or an extension.
False; plain def path operations are supported.
